transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Lin Zhao (Redwood SE), Elliot Shaw (CTO, VegaQuant), Priya Kapoor (Head of Security), Samir Desai (Infra Lead), Noah Klein (DevOps)

--- Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect) ---
VegaQuant is evaluating Redwood for low-latency trading signals. Primary concerns: proof of SOC2/ISO, SSO integration (SAML + SCIM), RBAC mapping to their AD groups, audit logging retention for 7 years, KMS BYOK with HSM, and options for Dedicated vs Private due to latency and regulatory controls.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have a full house from vegaquant, appreciate you making time, um quick intros...
00:10 Elliot: hi, elliot here, cto, we run a quant infra and, uh, low-latency inference pipelines, looking at redwood for inference serving across clouds
00:18 Priya: priya here, head of security, i'll be driving compliance questions
00:22 Samir: samir, infra, focus on network and deployment constraints
00:27 Maya: great, i'll do the redwood context, carlos is our se and will dig into the technicals, lin will jump on security-specific follow-ups

02:05 Carlos: quick agenda, 1) gauge your compliance needs, 2) talk hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private), 3) KMS/keys, SSO, RBAC and audit logs 4) next steps

03:10 Elliot: high level — we have a production cutover window in q3, ideally by mid-july. Success criteria: sub-50ms p99 for token generation on our critical model, deterministic throughputs and predictability for market hours; and of course compliance box checks completed by procurement

04:02 Priya: to add, we require SOC2 type II and ISO27001 evidence, we need SAML SSO with SCIM for provisioning, RBAC that maps to our AD groups, audit log retention for at least 7 years (some finance regs), and KMS with BYOK and HSM-backed keys, plus key rotation controls and export controls

05:12 Maya: makes sense. just to align, our hosted API is fastest to start but is multitenant — we have SOC2, ISO artifacts, and strict controls, but you might prefer dedicated for isolation and predictable latency. private deployment (VPC or on-prem) is available if you need complete network isolation and customer-managed control plane

06:00 Samir: question on hosted — can you do BYOK? we need the ability to retain control of keys so that data at rest is encrypted with customer keys, and they must be HSM backed.

06:15 Lin: short answer: hosted supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations for supported clouds and we have an EKM path for an HSM-backed solution; there are some limitations around cross-region key wrapping for older models but newer infra supports explicit BYOK for S3 and persistent caches. we'll share the exact matrix in the SOC/crypto doc

07:20 Noah: where are audit logs stored for hosted? can we ship them to our SIEM?

07:28 Carlos: yes, we stream audit logs and usage events to customer destinations; for hosted we can forward logs to your S3 bucket or to SIEM via syslog/secure collector. retention defaults are 90 days in the console but we support export and archiving to your long-term buckets for 7+ years; there is an export job and a lifecycle policy you can configure

08:10 Priya: is there an immutable audit trail? regulator expects tamper-evident logs for financial ops

08:18 Lin: we support signed append-only logs and can integrate with your S3 object lock and WORM policies; for dedicated or private deployments you can enable in-cluster append-only logging with HSM signing, or stream directly to your audit endpoint to ensure immutability

09:05 Elliot: for dedicated, is the control plane still hosted by redwood or customer-managed? concerns about metadata leaving our VPC

09:15 Maya: dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool and tenancy isolation, but the control plane remains Redwood-managed by default; however we offer private control plane options for enterprise customers where the control plane sits in your VPC and you manage network egress, credentials, and so forth — that's the Private offering

10:00 Samir: how about RBAC — we have fine-grained roles and need mapping to AD groups and service accounts for automation

10:12 Carlos: we offer RBAC with role templates and can sync to SAML/SCIM for group mappings; you can map AD groups to Redwood roles and even define custom policies for route/model-level access. we'll demo the RBAC UI and the SCIM group provisioning in the deep dive

12:00 Priya: do you provide separation across tenants for KV cache, model artifacts, and logs? we can't risk cross-tenant leakage

12:12 Lin: yes, in Dedicated we run tenant isolation at the GPU pool level and use namespace isolation for caches. Artifacts are stored in encrypted buckets with per-tenant encryption keys. For Hosted there are strong logical separations and encryption per tenant but if you need absolute physical separation we recommend Dedicated with private control plane

14:20 Elliot: about data retention — we have a 7-year retention mandate for raw inference inputs for auditability; is storing raw prompts default behavior? we want the option to disable storing prompts entirely

14:36 Carlos: by default we retain conversation data for 30-90 days for debugging and quality, but we offer configurable retention policies including immediate non-persistence (no logs stored) or a custom retention window. For regulatory needs we can set up direct export to your archive and/or ensure non-persistence in hosted mode if required

15:15 Priya: and encryption in transit — do you support mutual TLS? we have mTLS between our services and inference endpoints

15:24 Lin: yes, we support mTLS and can provision client certs for secure connections. In Dedicated and Private you can enforce strict mTLS and internal CA chains

16:40 Samir: key rotation — we need 90-day rotation with audit records and the ability to force revoke keys and re-encrypt persisted caches; how is that handled?

16:52 Lin: we integrate with your KMS for rotation policies. For caches and persisted state we support envelope encryption — if you rotate customer master key, we can trigger rewrap operations for persisted objects; for in-flight caches it's a bit trickier — we typically phase caches and allow for TTL-based eviction plus a re-encryption pass if needed. we'll document the operational runbook

18:10 Elliot: compliance evidence — we need SOC2 type II report and ISO27001 certificate, plus pen test summary and architecture diagrams for procurement

18:22 Maya: we have a redacted SOC2 type II report and ISO cert we can share under NDA, along with our security whitepaper and SOC/crypto matrix. i'll attach those to the follow-up email

19:00 Priya: for SSO, do you support IdP-initiated flows and Just-in-Time provisioning? we rely on SCIM for deprovisioning automation

19:12 Carlos: yes, both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML flows are supported; SCIM provisioning supports provisioning and deprovisioning of users and groups. we also support custom attribute mappings so you can map AD attributes to roles/policies

21:00 Noah: curious about network egress — in hosted mode where egress goes out of — is it redwood managed IP ranges? we need to add to our allow lists for market externalities

21:10 Maya: hosted egress uses Redwood-managed ranges and we'll share the ip ranges; for Dedicated you can use VPC peering and private routing to avoid internet egress; private deployment keeps egress under your control entirely

22:30 Priya: regulatory: do you support data residency and region locking? some of our customers require EU-only storage

22:38 Lin: yes, we support region locking for assets and model serving. For Hosted we have region-specific endpoints and data residency controls. Dedicated can be provisioned in a specific region and Private gives you full control to deploy in your region or on-prem

24:00 Elliot: one more — if we run a POC on Dedicated, can we run a micro-benchmark inside our VPC or do you require agent access?

24:12 Carlos: we can provision a dedicated slice and run benchmarks from your VPC via peering, or we can run a customer-provided load generator. For the POC we usually share an example repo with scripts and sample traffic profiles. We'll include seq length distributions to mirror trading use cases

26:40 Samir: SLAs — what's the uptime and latency SLO for Dedicated vs Hosted?

26:48 Maya: Hosted has standard availability and we publish metrics; Dedicated carries SLA-backed uptime and latency SLOs for committed capacity. Private SLA depends on the installation model but we provide operational playbooks for on-prem installs. We'll provide the SLA matrix in the follow-up

29:00 Priya: about pen testing — do you support customer-led pen tests against Hosted? we may need to run an annual assessment

29:10 Lin: for Hosted we have a controlled pen test program and allow customer-coordinated tests by arrangement. For Dedicated and Private you can run tests per the contract and we'll coordinate a pre-test scope and schedule

31:20 Elliot: can you explain how model updates are handled? we need a stable model pinning and a rollback path in case of regressions

31:32 Carlos: we support model version pinning per route and can do canary rollouts, A/B tests and automatic fallbacks to previous model revision on failure. Evals and canyon testing can be attached to a rollout so you can block a release on perf regressions

33:45 Samir: curious about billing / metering — we need token-level billing and per-route metrics for chargeback

33:55 Maya: console provides token-level breakdowns, per-model, per-route, and per-token-type cost insights. We can also stream usage events to your billing pipelines for chargeback

36:00 Priya: any outstanding gaps from a security perspective you see based on what i described?

36:10 Lin: nothing blocker; the main ask is ensuring we can meet your BYOK/HSM expectations and audit log tamper-proofing for 7 years. Those are supported in Dedicated/Private with the right contract and control plane options. Hosted can meet many needs but we'd want to confirm the exact KMS vendor and HSM requirements for compatibility

37:45 Elliot: timeline recap: mid-july production target. next steps are SOC/ISO docs, run a dedicated POC bench in your infra, and an architecture deep dive

38:00 Maya: yep, i'll attach the docs. carlos will own the bench repo and lin will own the security runbook. can we set tentative deep dive for next thursday?

38:12 Priya: next thursday works, we'll invite our procurement and legal for the procurement Qs

40:20 Carlos: i'll circulate a POC readme with steps — quick note, for the dedicated slice we need an allowlist of ip ranges and an SSH jump host for the initial setup; also ask you to share the model artifact size and expected token distribution

42:15 Samir: i'll share our infra diagram and the model artifact (it's about 3.2GB, 8k context), token distribution is spiky during market open — many short sequences, some long runs for re-eval cycles

44:00 Maya: any procurement constraints — special contract language for indemnity or data residency?

44:10 Priya: we'll have legal draft markups around data residency and encryption key control, possibly an addendum for private control plane if needed

46:00 Elliot: curious — have you had customers in finserv with 7-year log retention? if so, how did you handle cost and tape-archival workflows

46:12 Lin: yes, a couple. pattern is stream logs to customer S3 with lifecycle to Glacier/Deep Archive, and keep an index in a low-cost DB for quick lookup. We supply a retention automation playbook to be included in the engagement

48:30 Maya: ok recap: 1) Maya send SOC2/ISO docs under NDA, 2) Carlos share POC repo and benchmark plan, 3) Samir share infra diag and model artifacts, 4) schedule 2-hr deep dive next Thursday. Anything else?

48:50 Priya: also need a redacted pen-test summary and list of third-party vendors used in hosted control plane

49:05 Maya: will include pen test summary and vendor list in the pack. Anything else from vegaquant?

50:20 Elliot: no, that's good. thanks, everyone.

50:30 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invite

--- End Transcript ---
